issue.body:
## Bug

On Windows, the "Open in editor" (`IDE ↗`) topbar control cannot open the session workspace in Cursor, VS Code, or any other editor — even when those editors are installed. The control reports no supported editors found, so the primary button is permanently disabled.

**Source:** reported in Discord `#bug-triage` | **Reported by:** @Vaibhaav-Tiwari | **Analyzed against:** `9997248c4` (origin/main, 2026-09-01)
**Confidence:** Medium — mechanism traced in code and consistent with the report; the reporter's machine has not been probed (see "Open questions").

## Reproduction

1. Windows 10/11, AO desktop ≥ v0.12.10 (feature landed in d2fec68c2, Aug 23 — shipped in v0.12.10).
2. Install Cursor and/or VS Code with default installer options (User Installer — the default on Windows — does **not** add `bin` to PATH unless "Add to PATH" is checked; the `cursor`/`code` shims live under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\...`).
3. Open any local session → look at the topbar `IDE ↗` control.
4. Actual: primary button disabled; dropdown shows no editors; guidance: *"No supported editor found. Use File Explorer or Command Prompt, or install Cursor."* — despite Cursor/VS Code being installed.
5. Expected: Cursor / VS Code detected and clickable.

## Root Cause

Editor detection on Windows is a **PATH-only scan with no fallback probing** — while macOS gets an explicit app-bundle fallback and Linux gets hardcoded extra dirs.

`frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.ts`:

- `commandSearchDirs()` (lines 92–96): for `win32` it returns **only** `env.PATH` split entries. Compare: darwin appends `/opt/homebrew/bin` etc., linux appends `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`. There is no Windows equivalent.
- `resolveEditor()` (lines 112–128): after the PATH scan misses, the `.app` bundle fallback (lines 122–127) is gated behind `if (deps.platform !== "darwin") return undefined;` — so on Windows detection ends at "not installed."
- `EDITOR_CANDIDATES` (lines 27–47): each candidate has exactly one `commands[]` entry (`cursor`, `code`, `windsurf`, …). The standard Windows install locations are never probed:
  - VS Code / VS Code Insiders / Cursor / Windsurf user installs: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\{Microsoft VS Code,Cursor,Windsurf}\bin\{code,cursor,windsurf}.cmd` (also `{version}\bin` layout for VS Code)
  - System installs: `%ProgramFiles%\...\bin`
  - JetBrains Toolbox: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\Toolbox\scripts\` (`idea.cmd`, `webstorm.cmd`, …)
  - Windows `App Paths` registry (`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\code.exe`) — the OS-blessed lookup that `ShellExecute`/`start` use
- On Windows the CLIs are `.cmd` shims, not `.exe` — `executableNames()` (lines 86–90) does handle PATHEXT expansion for names *within a search dir*, so this is not the failure; the failure is that the *dirs themselves* are PATH-only.
- Additionally, `createEditorHandoff()` (lines 163–165) resolves the editor list **once at module construction** (wired at `frontend/src/main.ts:699`). If PATH/environment differs at launch (e.g. app auto-started, or user installs an editor later and doesn't restart AO), the list is stale for the entire app lifetime.

Renderer behavior when detection finds nothing — `frontend/src/renderer/components/TopbarOpenEditorButton.tsx`:

- Line 88: `const mainDisabled = busy || !workspaceAvailable || !preferred;` — with `editors.length === 0`, `preferred` is `undefined` → primary button permanently disabled.
- Lines 96–99: shows `editor.noEditorGuidance` → *"No supported editor found. Use File Explorer or Command Prompt, or install Cursor."* — misleading on a machine where Cursor **is** installed.
- Note `DEFAULT_EDITOR_ID = "cursor"` (`frontend/src/main/editor-settings.ts:6`), so the default preference is also among the "not found" set.

Not the cause (verified): the launch path handles Windows shims correctly — `frontend/src/main/launch-command.ts` `spawnSpec()` wraps `.cmd`/`.bat` via `cmd.exe /d /s /c` with `windowsVerbatimArguments`. The gap is purely **detection/resolution**, and secondarily the misleading guidance.

This mirrors the class of issue the feature's own spec called out (#3118 acceptance criteria: *"Failures are visible (not silent); works when app launched from Dock"* — the Windows analog, "works when app launched without the editor's shims on PATH," is unmet).

## Fix Direction

1. Add Windows fallback search roots in `commandSearchDirs()` / `resolveEditor()`:
   - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\*` per-candidate `bin` dirs (match on `{code,cursor,windsurf,...}.cmd`), `{Version}\bin` for VS Code family
   - `%ProgramFiles%`, `%ProgramFiles(x86)%` install roots
   - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\Toolbox\scripts`
   - Optionally `App Paths` registry lookup via `reg query` (keeps it dependency-free)
2. Keep PATH-first ordering so an explicit PATH install wins over a probed one.
3. Re-resolve editor targets per `getState()` call (or cache with TTL) instead of freezing at app start, so a mid-session install or environment change is picked up.
4. If zero editors are detected on win32 after probing, keep the File Explorer/Terminal fallbacks but improve guidance (e.g. "Open {worktree} in File Explorer" is already there; the "install Cursor" line should not be the only hint when the editor may merely be off-PATH).
5. Add `win32` coverage to `frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.test.ts` (currently zero win32 cases) covering: shim in PATH, shim only in `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, PATHEXT expansion, and none-found.

## Impact

- All Windows users whose editor CLI shims are not on the GUI process's PATH (default User Installer path for VS Code; common for Cursor when "Add to PATH" was skipped) cannot use the `IDE ↗` feature at all — the feature is effectively macOS/Linux-only for them.
- The error guidance blames a missing install, sending users to reinstall editors that are already present.

## Open questions (from the reporter's machine)

- Exact AO version and whether the dropdown shows *some* editors or none (distinguishes "PATH miss for all" vs "partial detection").
- Whether Cursor/VS Code were installed per-user (`%LOCALAPPDATA%`) or system-wide.
- Terminal/File Explorer targets (which don't depend on PATH for file-manager, and use `ComSpec` for terminal) presumably still work — worth confirming the report is editor-specific.

## Related

- #3118 — feature spec: "Open session worktree in external IDE (`IDE ↗` + target menu)"
- #4571 — cloud-session gating for the same control (d2a134db7)
- #4607 — Neovim target request (same surface)
